amendment.prompted_by: v3-2 was recorded as PASS_PROVISIONAL (docs/receipts/validation/optomotor-yaw-v3-2.md) only because its five gating physiology bounds were marked verified:false. The owner passed Phase 1 provisionally on 2026-09-25 and asked for those bounds to be checked against primary sources.
changes: DNa02 (checks P1-P3) is now verified from recordings: spontaneous 0-20 -> 0-40 Hz (Yang et al. 2024 Fig. S7A, not-walking per-fly means 7.8-38.5 Hz; Rayshubskiy et al. 2025 deposited recordings), driven 0-100 -> 0-150 Hz (Yang et al. 2024: a ~15 spikes/s modulation is ~10% of the cell's dynamic range; the busiest 1 s bins in the Rayshubskiy recordings reach 93-128 Hz). Derivation: validation/specs/sources/dna02_rates_read.json.

brain_mean (P6) and brain_max_single_neuron (P7) keep their numbers (0-5 Hz, 0-300 Hz) but are declared model-health limits instead of physiological claims: no primary source measures either quantity in the fly. They are marked kind: model_health and verified: true in the same sense as the causal-control gates O5-O7 (a check on the model itself, not a literature value); see the bounds file.
Seeds 100-105 -> 200-205, so a run of this spec is a new replication.
amendment.unchanged: Every behaviour gate, threshold and target; stimulus, schedule, encoder, decoder, conditions, controls, the reported items, analysis and decision rule.
amendment.blinding: The bounds were chosen from the literature without opening the v3-1 or v3-2 receipts or records. What was known: v3-2 passed all five physiology checks against the v2 bounds, and v3-1 failed only on HS. Because v3 only widens the DNa02 intervals and leaves the brain limits unchanged, it cannot turn a pass under v2 into a fail; readers should weigh that the change was made knowing the v2 checks had passed.
amendment.what_readers_should_weigh: No DNa02 recording during visual motion was found: every read DNa02 rate comes from walking flies in the dark or with odour or heat. The driven bound is therefore the cell's recorded range in any state, not an optomotor-specific range. The brain-wide limits catch runaway activity; they do not test physiology.

summary: Open-loop (tethered) optomotor yaw on the full MaleCNS graph under LIF v3: does rotation of a full-field grating in either direction, at full and half contrast, produce syndirectional steering through DNa02, and are the firing rates on the way physiological? Third version: an independent replication with new seeds, against bounds v3, in which DNa02 is verified from recordings and the brain-wide limits are declared model-health checks.
supersedes_for_v3: docs/wp5_optomotor_prereg.json (v1 protocol). Stimulus, encoder, decoder, schedule, seeds and controls are copied from it unchanged; the gates are new and literature-anchored.
backend: auto (GPU when a CUDA device is usable, CPU otherwise); recorded in the receipt

stimulus.blocks_format: [direction s, contrast]; s=+1 = pattern rotates counter-clockwise seen from above (leftward)
stimulus.literature_match: Duistermars 2007 used 30 deg periods (flight); Mano 2023 used 60 deg at 1 Hz (walking). 1.5 Hz lies on the rising flank of the flight TF curve (plateau 3-10 Hz), so only the SIGN and presence of the response are gated, never its size.

encoder.populations: T4a+T5a (front-to-back) and T4b+T5b (back-to-front) per eye, matched counts, lowest source IDs; pinned OPTOMOTOR_IO_PIN
encoder.assumption: direction selectivity is supplied by the encoder (Maisak 2013 subtype directions), not computed by the graph

decoder.note: the gain is a unit conversion, not fitted; absolute yaw magnitudes are therefore not comparable to fly turning speeds and are reported only

seed_role: encoder per-cell phases and per-step noise; the network starts from rest in every trial

analysis.response: R = mean over the named blocks of s_b * (mean decoded yaw in block b); the whole 1 s block is the window (Mano 2023: syndirectional for ~1 s even at high contrast)

gates.claim: Turning index over all blocks is syndirectional (95% CI above 0).
gates.basis: published: flies turn with the direction of full-field rotation

gates.claim: Leftward rotation (s=+1) alone evokes leftward yaw.
gates.basis: published: syndirectional to rotation in either direction; guards against the one-sided WP5 v1 result

gates.claim: Rightward rotation (s=-1) alone evokes rightward yaw.

gates.basis: published: syndirectional at contrast 0.25 throughout, early response plateaus near 0.5 contrast (walking)

gates.claim: Intact minus sham (encoder runs, nothing delivered), paired by seed, above 0.
gates.basis: causal control of the model itself; not a literature value

gates.claim: Intact minus degree-preserving shuffled graph, paired by seed, above 0.
gates.basis: causal control of the model itself; not a literature value

gates.claim: With both DNa02 clamped, decoded yaw is exactly 0 at every step of every seed.
gates.basis: causal control of the model itself; not a literature value

reported.claim: Half-contrast response is at least 0.7 of the full-contrast response (plateau near 0.5 contrast).
reported.basis: Mano 2023 plateau statement; the 0.7 cut-off is a judgement, so this is reported, not gated

reported.claim: TI in rad/s (decoder units; no biological magnitude claim).

reported.note: reported for information only; not part of the verdict (see amendment)
reported for information only; not part of the verdict (see amendment)

decision_rule: Behaviour PASS iff every gate passes. Physiology PASS iff every check lies in its bound. Verdict PASS iff both pass on a confirmatory run (real graph, this spec committed and unchanged, these seeds, clean tree); PASS_PROVISIONAL if any gating value is marked unverified; FAIL if any gate or check fails; INCONCLUSIVE if one cannot be evaluated. Full rule: validation/harness.py VERDICTS.

duistermars2007.citation: Duistermars BJ, Chow DM, Condro M, Frye MA (2007) The spatial, temporal and contrast properties of expansion and rotation flight optomotor responses in Drosophila. J Exp Biol 210(18):3218
values_read: flight rotation responses consistent 0.1-0.6 Hz, rise steeply to a plateau at 3-10 Hz, roll off at 30 Hz (Results, Fig. 3)
optomotor responses reach steady state within roughly 1 s (Methods)

mano2023.citation: Mano O, et al., Clark DA (2023) Long-timescale anti-directional rotation in Drosophila optomotor behavior. eLife 12:e86076
mano2023.read: full text (eLife); author list beyond first and last not verified
values_read: walking flies, 60 deg wavelength, 1 Hz: high-contrast gratings evoke syndirectional turning for ~1 s, then reversal (Fig. 1b)
contrast 0.25: syndirectional throughout the 5 s stimulus (Fig. 1b)
early turning speed rises with contrast, plateau around 0.5 contrast (Fig. 1c)

maisak2013.citation: Maisak MS, et al., Borst A (2013) A directional tuning map of Drosophila elementary motion detectors. Nature 500:212-216
values_read: T4/T5 subtypes a-d respond to front-to-back, back-to-front, upward, downward motion (encoder assumption, inherited from WP5)

rayshubskiy2025.citation: Rayshubskiy A, et al., Wilson RI (2025) eLife 13:RP102230 (preprint bioRxiv 2020.04.04.024703)
rayshubskiy2025.read: text; no absolute DNa02 firing rates in the text (figures only)
values_read: DNa02 activity predicts and unilateral activation evokes ipsilateral turning (decoder convention, inherited from WP5)

schnell2010.citation: Schnell B, Joesch M, Forstner F, Raghu SV, Otsuna H, Ito K, Borst A, Reiff DF (2010) Processing of horizontal optic flow in three visual interneurons of the Drosophila brain. J Neurophysiol 103:1646-1657
values_read: first whole-cell recordings from HSN, HSE and HSS; excited by front-to-back, inhibited by back-to-front motion

joesch2008.citation: Joesch M, Plett J, Borst A, Reiff DF (2008) Response properties of motion-sensitive visual interneurons in the lobula plate of Drosophila melanogaster. Curr Biol 18:368-374
joesch2008.doi_status: title matched by search (PubMed 18328703, ScienceDirect S096098220800167X)

fujiwara2017.citation: Fujiwara T, Cruz TL, Bohnslav JP, Chiappe ME (2017) A faithful internal representation of walking movements in the Drosophila visual system. Nat Neurosci 20 (pages not checked)
fujiwara2017.doi_status: title and DOI matched by search (nature.com, PubMed 27798632)
